CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney screening in patient with Smith-Magenis Syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old female twin, former 34 and 3-week gestation infant, presenting for kidney evaluation. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis Syndrome following failure to sit independently by 12 months of age and delay in achieving independent ambulation. Birth weight was approximately 4 pounds 8 ounces; her twin sister weighed 3 pounds 13 ounces at birth. As a newborn, she experienced apneic episodes during feeding and difficulty with temperature regulation. She has a history of significant gastroesophageal reflux managed by gastroenterology and was transitioned from cow's milk to pea protein milk (Ripple) per dietician recommendation. Currently receiving feeding therapy, occupational therapy, and physical therapy, with speech therapy to begin within the next couple of weeks. Multiple specialists have been involved including gastroenterology, allergy, neurology, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. Genetics counselor discussed that Smith-Magenis Syndrome can be associated with kidney fusion and orthopedic complications. Current voiding is 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours. Fluid intake includes pea protein milk, water, and occasional diluted juice. She is now crawling and attempting to take steps. Twin sister is healthy and unaffected. Family resides in Dallas, Georgia.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis Syndrome, prematurity at 34 and 3 weeks gestation, gastroesophageal reflux disease, developmental delay.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother, age 9, with autism diagnosis. Denies family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or transplant.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Resides in Dallas, Georgia with 9-year-old brother with autism and unaffected female twin sister.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes appear small. Mild hypotonia noted in lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs normal. Ears normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week gestation twin with Smith-Magenis Syndrome. The syndrome is associated with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT). Kidney ultrasound is to be performed today for screening. If ultrasound results are normal, no further nephrology follow-up is needed. If abnormalities are identified, further evaluation and management will be determined. Given family residence in Dallas, Georgia, future follow-up will be arranged at the Kennesaw location if needed.
